subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should hook-triggered agent sessions gain a dedicated lifecycle policy, and should the first supported contract be retention-only or include immediate deletion and transcript archival?
rationale: Current main clearly lacks the capability, but storage safety, audit retention, multi-turn hook compatibility, defaults, and the acceptable size of a new config surface require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Start with safe retention
options.body: Add a hook-specific age-based retention policy with current preserve-forever behavior as the default, leaving immediate deletion and archival for later evidence-backed work.

options.title: Implement full lifecycle modes
options.body: Add preserve, delayed cleanup, and on-complete disposal together with explicit transcript keep, delete, or archive semantics and precedence rules.

options.title: Use generic maintenance only
options.body: Decline a hook-specific surface, document generic session maintenance as the supported mechanism, and close this request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Start with safe retention
recommendation.body: Add a hook-specific age-based retention policy with current preserve-forever behavior as the default, leaving immediate deletion and archival for later evidence-backed work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest combined signal from feature history and the existing issue discussion for choosing the permanent core/config contract.
